item.title: Low-Earth Orbit
item.description: Last week I came across this very high-quality image, at first I thought that it must be one of those expensive satellites that cost millions of dollars. Then I started digging and found out how ignorant i am about the recent advances in satellites. Apparently, there are three main orbits used by current satellites [1]: LEO (Low Earth Orbit): ~160–2,000 km; short orbital period (90–120 min); low latency; used for Earth observation, Starlink, ISS.
